## B. Atty. Ronald A. Ramos (defense counsel), on-record items only

**Record facts.**

- **R1. Court warning, 11 Mar 2026** (ORD p.2): "Atty. Ramos is warned, that further filing of incorrect pleadings which in effect disrupt court processes shall warrant appropriate sanction. No further liberality shall be accorded."
  - Compliance followed (ORD p.3).
  - On 4 Sep 2026 the court noted "both counsels timely compliance" (ORD p.4).
- **R2. Attestation date mismatch on Erwin's JA.** The counsel attestation reads "APR 01" (year read by OCR as "2006"), while the affiant's jurat reads "APR 04 2026" (JA-E p.6) [VERIFY on the original].
- **R3. Gloria's JA.**
  - Examined "sa pamamagitan ng video conferencing" (JA-G p.2).
  - The affiant jurat is blank in the file copy.
  - Ramos's attestation is subscribed 12 May 2026 at Daet (JA-G p.14).
  - The JA was excluded at pre-trial; a "scanned copy" was presented (MAN ¶1).
- **R4. "Summary Procedure"** stated in MAN ¶¶2, 20, against ORD p.1.

**Text:**

- **JAR §4:** the attestation must state that counsel "faithfully recorded or caused to be recorded the questions he asked and the corresponding answers that the witness gave" and that no one "coached the witness". **§4(b):** "A false attestation shall subject the lawyer mentioned to disciplinary action, including disbarment."
- **JAR §10(c):** "The court shall not admit as evidence judicial affidavits that do not conform to the content requirements of Section 3 and the attestation requirement of Section 4 above. The court may, however, allow only once the subsequent submission of the compliant replacement affidavits …"
- **CPRA Canon III §2:** "A lawyer shall uphold the constitution, obey the laws of the land, promote respect for laws and legal processes …" (chanrobles [VERIFY]).
- **CPRA Canon II §8:** "A lawyer shall not misquote, misrepresent, or mislead the court as to the existence or the contents of any document, argument, evidence, law, or other legal authority … or assert as a fact that which has not been proven." [VERIFY against the SC text.]
- **CPRA §33(p):** a serious offense is "Violation of the notarial rules, except reportorial requirements, when attended by bad faith".
- **CPRA §34(a):** a less serious offense is "Simple misconduct, or such misconduct without the manifest elements of corruption, clear intent to violate the law or flagrant disregard of established rules".
- **2004 Notarial Rules, Rule II §6 (Jurat):** the individual "(a) appears in person before the notary public … (c) signs the instrument or document in the presence of the notary; and (d) takes an oath or affirmation before the notary public".

**Elements against the record:**

- **R1.** The court has already dealt with it, and later recorded compliance (ORD pp.3–4). There is no basis for a separate complaint. **Does not fit.**
- **R2.** Counsel's attestation is a sworn statement by counsel. Under the Notarial Rules, his own jurat for the attestation is a separate notarial act.
  - A 1 Apr attestation can be true if the examination was completed by then, even if the affiant swore on 4 Apr.
  - A "false attestation" under JAR §4(b) needs the content of the attestation to be untrue, not merely an earlier date.
  - The record does not show the content was untrue. **Does not fit as a disciplinary matter.**
  - In court: possible JAR §10(c) objection material, with the original checked first.
- **R3.** The examination by videoconference is disclosed on the face of the JA (JA-G p.2), and the court has already excluded the JA.
  - Whether Gloria's own oath was properly taken abroad is a question about the affiant's jurat and its notary or consul, not about Ramos's attestation. Remote notarization rules (A.M. 20-07-04-SC) were not read [VERIFY].
  - **Does not fit as to Ramos on the record.**
- **R4.** This is an advocacy position on which rule governs. The court's own order is in the record. It does not on its face assert an unproven fact. **Does not fit** [rate LOW].

**Evidence missing:**

- the originals of the JA-E and JA-G jurats and attestations;
- the notarial register entries of the notary "… MORALES", commission "2025-37"/"2026-37" (JA-E p.6; JA-G p.14) [VERIFY the name];
- the 13 May 2026 pre-trial order or TSN on why the JA was excluded.

**Risk to 26-360:**

- A complaint against opposing counsel during trial is the clearest "retaliation" signal to the court.
- It risks CPRA Canon II §13 ("in the absence of factual or legal basis") if the originals show regular dates.
- It invites a reciprocal look at our own JAs: the Exh. L/M/N jurat/commission check is still open (DL).

**Recommendation:**

- **Never** as IBP or SC discipline on the present record. Rating: LOW.
- **Now, in court only:** Barandon may raise R2 and R3 as admissibility objections under JAR §10(c), and in the comment on MAN, after checking the originals.
- **After judgment:** no action, unless the originals show an attestation whose content is untrue. Even then, only on Barandon's assessment.
